Absolute temperature equals Celsius reading plus 273.15; 37.3 °C converts numerically to 310.45 K before rounding. A displayed tenth-degree reading does not warrant hundredth-degree measurement precision.
For the stipulated fixed gas model, absolute temperatures scale as squared speed ratios; the supplied values give approximately 48 °C. Same-gas/medium assumptions required.

Water density has a maximum near 4 °C; if melting cools the water below this temperature, the total liquid volume rises relative to displaced mass at 4 °C. If final water returns to 4 °C and vessel unchanged, no rise. Publisher key A preserved; final thermal conditions require independent adjudication.

Transverse motion of string and airborne longitudinal sound differ; common frequency does not imply equal wavelength.
